title: Running a cafe
summary: Keeps the outlet's sales, purchases, menu and stock in one place, compares each day with the last, sums up the week, and says when a dish costs too much or stock runs low.

asks.question: Which outlets do you run, and what are they called?
asks.why: So every number lands in the right outlet's rows.

asks.question: What food cost do you aim for, as a percentage of the price?
asks.why: To say when a dish costs more than you want it to.

homework.find: The outlet's public listing: address, opening hours, what it is known for.
The menu with its prices, from the outlet's own page or a delivery app.
Recent public reviews, and any nobody answered.

senses.describe: The daily sales report your till system can email
senses.ask: Your till can email its closing report every night. Shall I show you the address to send it to?

senses.describe: The statements your delivery apps send
senses.ask: Delivery apps email a statement of what they paid out. Forward them to me and I'll keep them with the sales.

senses.describe: The orders page of your delivery app's merchant site
senses.ask: If you sign in to your delivery app's merchant page with me once, I can keep an eye on new orders and ratings.
Forward supplier invoices to me and I'll keep ingredient prices up to date.

rhythms.do: Compare this day's net sales and transactions with the same weekday last week, per outlet. Mention the one item that moved most.
The week in three lines: net sales against the week before, the best and the weakest item, and anything over the food-cost target.
Update ingredient prices from the invoice and recheck the plate cost of the dishes that use them; say which went past the food-cost target.

signals.when: a dish costs more than 35 % of its price
signals.say: Name the dish, its food cost now, and what price or portion would bring it back.

check.sql: SELECT item, price, plate_cost, food_cost_pct FROM items WHERE food_cost_pct > 35 ORDER BY food_cost_pct DESC

signals.when: an item is under its par level
signals.say: Say what is low, at which outlet, and offer a reorder.

check.sql: SELECT outlet, item, on_hand, par, unit FROM levels WHERE on_hand < par

prepare.when: stock is under par and the usual supplier is known
prepare.describe: A reorder message to the usual supplier
